4. Defendant No. 1 filed a written statement stating that Plot No. 6302 is canal which is being used by the people of the locality. After the promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the said canal has been used by the villagers which was entrusted to the District Council for its management. It is asserted that Humayun Kabir, Younus Mia and others encroached some portion of the canal and trying to build market therein and some portion of the canal is being used as Baby Taxi stand. It is further asserted that with a view to cause loss to defendant No. 1 some elements have taken various devices and filed the instant suit with untrue averments and, as such, prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. Defendant No. 2, Government of Bangladesh filed written statement contending that the suit plot being canal has been recorded in the name of the government and it is being used by the local people. Some people of the locality encroached the canal and erected structure therein. When notices were issued against the illegal occupiers they took various pretext of having taken license from the District Council. It is further asserted that the suit land being part of khatian No. 1 it cannot be leased out by District Council without the permission of the concerned ministry. 

 6. Defendant No. 3 District Council filed a written statement, stating that, the suit plot is canal being used by the local people. After the promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the said canal brought into the Management of District Council which is managing the same. Plaintiff's elder brother, Humyun Kobir and others encroached upon the canal and erected market therein and there is also a Baby Taxi stand in some portion of the canal. The district Council leased out portion of it wherein Sawmill has been installed, other parts of the canal has been leased out to various persons. It is stated that plaintiffs are not entitled to get easement of necessity over the suit land. It is further stated that on 12-11-2003 portions of the canal has been leased out to 22 persons and, as such, prayed for dismissal of suit. 

 12. So far the locus standi of the present petitioners of filing the instant revisional application is concerned it appears that they were not parties in the original proceeding. They did not file written statement and did not examine witnesses. It is apparent that they are licensees or lessees from the District Council. It is found that the District Council has no authority to lease out canal which obstructed free flow of water and, as such, as licensee or lessee, as the case may be, the present petitioners have no locus standi to file instant revisional application.
